errors.evidence: The description incorrectly maps the colors to the categories. According to the legend, 'Equivalence-One-Easy' is the second darkest blue, 'Equivalence-One-Hard' is the third shade (a medium blue), and 'Equivalence-All-Easy' is the fourth shade (a light blue). The description scrambles this order.

errors.text_span: The data reveals a consistent trend where success rates decrease as the perturbation type becomes more complex
errors.evidence: The phrase 'becomes more complex' is an interpretation of the relationship between the categories ('Seed', 'Equivalence-One-Easy', etc.). It is not explicitly stated in the chart and violates the instruction to avoid interpretation.
For the 'Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code)' model, the bar for 'Equivalence-All-Hard' reaches approximately 65%, not 70%.
The phrase 'sharp decline' is interpretive and subjective language. The prompt requires objective description of values.

errors.text_span: This pattern is observed across most models, highlighting a substantial drop in performance even for models that perform well on the baseline 'Seed' set.
errors.evidence: This sentence draws a conclusion and uses interpretive language ('substantial drop in performance'), which is explicitly forbidden by the prompt. It synthesizes information to make a point, rather than just describing the visual elements.
The description fails to mention the tick label interval for the y-axis (every 20 units), which was a specific requirement of the generation prompt.
